title: Horizon and Compass
premise: Yara Pemberton, estranged son of the late archaeologist Dr. Elias Pemberton, is salvaging his father's abandoned river concession when the floodwater coughs up a bronze chest bearing the seal of a nation that no longer exists. The find triggers a race against expiring permits, a rival salvage crew, and the monsoon itself, forcing Yara to partner with Noor, a river pilot who knew his father better than he did. As the chest's contents reveal that Elias deliberately hid evidence of a living descendant community — not a dead civilization — Yara must choose between publishing the discovery that would make his name and honoring the inheritance of people the maps erased. He chooses the people, burning the permits' claim, and in doing so finally understands the father he resented.
about_author: Petra Almeida is a former field surveyor who spent six seasons mapping waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels where landscapes are characters and every treasure comes with a debt attached.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Arriving at his father's derelict riverside camp to settle the estate, Yara finds the concession permit expiring in thirty days and the dig site looted. When the swollen river exposes a sealed bronze chest stamped with an extinct nation's crest, he realizes his father died chasing it. Emotional beat: grief curdling into stubborn curiosity.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Boat
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A river pilot with her own debts to Elias, Noor agrees to ferry Yara upstream through rising waters, but only if he shares whatever the chest holds. Its first compartment reveals survey maps marking villages that officially never existed. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two people both abandoned by the same man.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The rival salvage crew, backed by the concession company, boards them mid-river; a storm wrecks the boat and the chest cracks open, revealing letters proving the 'lost' civilization survived as a hidden river community Elias protected by burying his own findings. Emotional beat: love against duty — Yara torn between fame and his father's silence.

chapters.title: Horizon and Compass
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With hours left on the permits, Yara reaches the descendant village, confronts what his father chose over glory, and lets the rival crew salvage an empty chest while he files the site as protected ancestral land. He and Noor stay through the monsoon's end. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — not what we take, but what we refuse to sell.
